newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala power plant sale delayed.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala power plant sale delayed.

text.p: Bids from eleven companies interested in buying two Guatemalan electric plants will be opened Aug. 13 instead of July 30, an official said on Tuesday.
"The date was set back as a consequence of petitions from the bidders," Fernando Garcia, of the Guatemalan Electric Company (EEGSA), told Reuters.
Garcia said the bidders asked for changes in some "tough" conditions such as the terms of punishment when a generator breaks down during peak hours.
The changes were made and bidders were given more time to turn in final documents.
Eleven different companies and consortiums qualified to bid and submitted offers to purchase the two thermoelectric plants, with a combined capacity of 80 megawatts.
Bidding is closed and Garcia said EEGSA will choose the winning bid on the same day the offers are opened.

The firms are AES Americas Inc., of Arlington, Virginia.; C.A. Electricidad of Caracas; Coastal Power Co. of Houston with its subsidiary TICO; Constellation Power Development of Baltimore; Enron Caribe IV Ltd. of Houston; ENDESA Desarrollo of Spain; the consortium Energy Partners of Bethesda, Maryland; Marathon Power of Houston; Maxpower International of Marblehead, Massachusetts; ORMAT of Sparks, Nevada; and Union Fenosa of Spain.

EEGSA is selling the plants under the General Electricity Law passed by Congress in September, which demonopolizes electric production and allows new producers to sell electricity directly to consumers on the open market.
The law and this sale are part of Guatemala's sweeping privatization and demonopolization program.
The winning bid will offer the best package in terms of price per killowatt hour and capacity. The $30 million purchase price is set.

The firms are bidding on a Power Purchase Agreement to buy 90 percent of the assets. The remaining 10 percent, valued at an additional $3 million, will be held in reserve through the end of the year to allow employees to secure financing to purchase shares in the new company.
